subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for Windows shell expansions

question: Should Windows PowerShell expansion commands always require one-shot approval even when an existing exact-command allow-always grant matches?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes command-execution approval semantics for previously trusted Windows expansion commands, and automation cannot choose that security/compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Require One-Shot Expansion Approval
options.body: Patch gateway to match node-host behavior so expansion markers always force allow-once/deny and add the durable exact-command regression before merge.

options.title: Preserve Durable Trust
options.body: Keep existing exact-command allow-always semantics for expansion commands, but narrow the PR because it no longer matches the stated security boundary.

options.title: Pause For Policy Design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define a broader Windows exec approval policy for expansion-bearing commands.

recommendation.title: Require One-Shot Expansion Approval
recommendation.body: Patch gateway to match node-host behavior so expansion markers always force allow-once/deny and add the durable exact-command regression before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current command planner and approval persistence behavior being changed dates to jesse-merhi's Tree-sitter command authorization work.
